per_pair.why: B stages death as an event (impact, crack-web shatter, red bleed, a summary that types itself in), while A just tints the screen red and sits on a static GAME OVER/QUIT for nine of twelve frames.

B's summary names the cause and location of death, shows depth progress, a portrait, six readable stats, unlocked lore and clear R/E/Esc retry options; A is a sparse four-line stat panel on a mostly empty slate box.
B's victory banner is crisp and framed against a readable boss arena, while A's STAGE COMPLETED text is buried under a tangle of effect lines and gem clutter.

B's victory summary stacks a sunset palette shift, a full depth track, collected boons, records and lore into a cohesive celebratory screen; A adds a weapon row and an achievement toast but is still a plain list in a flat box.

B goes from summary to a new run with an arena title card in about one frame, while A drops to the title screen, press-to-start, the main menu and character select, and is still not back in play after twelve frames.

loser_biggest_gap: Replace the bare GAME OVER + QUIT overlay with a staged death beat (hit-stop, character death animation or shatter, camera push) that hands off to a summary with an immediate one-key Run Again, so the player is not routed back through the title screen and character select.
loser_other_gaps: Expand the results screen: give the cause and location of death, a progress or depth indicator, best and record comparisons, and something unlocked or learned, so it tells the story of the run.
Make victory readable: clear or dim the effect clutter behind the STAGE COMPLETED banner and give the win its own framing and palette, so it differs from the death screen.
Animate the end screens (stats counting up, panel slide-in) instead of a static result card on a flat red background.
Fill the dead space in the results panel and match its UI style (slate box, blue DONE button) to the in-game art direction.
reasoning: B treats both endings as authored events: a visible shatter on death, a distinct sunset-palette victory, and summaries that report the cause, progress, boons, records and lore, which makes the loop feel complete and gives a reason to go again. B is also built for replay, with Run Again and Same Seed on one key each and almost no delay before the next arena. A has the bones (a death state, a win state, a results list) but each one is a static, sparse overlay, its victory moment is hard to read, and play again takes a long menu trip through the title and character select. B still has rough edges: the death frames go dark and murky before the summary, the summary title is half-typed on its first frame, and the victory summary shows a debug-looking 'SHOWCASE: STAGED RUN HISTORY' label. Even so, B is clearly more polished across all five pairs.
